scale.1: 有问题（问题表里必须有对应条目）
scale.2: 基本没问题，有小瑕疵（写证据）

scoring.evidence_rule: 证据要指到句号 lNN / 屏号、原文或数字，至少 8 个字；没证据的高分按 0 处理。
scoring.disagreement: 单审：a 位评分即最终分。（双审时：两位同一维度差 ≥2，或一人 ≤1、另一人 ≥2，交裁决人；两人都 ≥2 的维度，裁决人每项抽 2 维复核。）

items.law_name: 中文口播（母语听感，盲审）
items.checks: 逐句听讲解员的中文：真人讲解会不会这么说、听一遍能不能懂。
items.how: 盲审：只听口播（按播放顺序）
items.what: 逐句听讲解员的中文：真人讲解会不会这么说、听一遍能不能懂。
items.problem: 上一版「本期内容」念成「这一期，讲四件事：它是个什么问题；为什么只背练习册不行……」，像在念目录，正常人不会这么说话（用户 2026-11-08 指出）；原先的审稿没抓到。
items.model_why: Claude 单审：a 位评分即最终分，不对比、不裁决

rubric.name: 像真人在讲
rubric.question: 逐句：自然 / 有点怪 / 很怪。书面腔、讲解腔、翻译腔、念稿感、报菜名式罗列都算怪

rubric.name: 衔接与过渡
rubric.question: 开场、本期内容、章节转换、举例前后：像一个人顺着思路往下讲，而不是「下面讲第一点」式的模板或目录朗读；上下句接得上

rubric.name: 一遍听懂
rubric.question: 只靠耳朵：一句只带一个新意思；指代清楚（说「这个」时观众知道指什么）；术语先解释再用；数字、同音字不会听错

rubric.name: 精炼
rubric.question: 没有废话、重复、正确的空话；删掉不影响理解的句子要指出来

rubric.name: 口吻与节奏
rubric.question: 从头到尾是同一个亲切、清楚、不端着的讲解者；长短句交替，每句适合一口气念完

rubric.name: 改写
rubric.question: 每句「有点怪 / 很怪」都给出可以直接替换、不更长的中文改写；列出最别扭的 5 句并排序

V1.evidence: 多数句子是真人口吻，如 l10「真的假的搅在一起，我们先把能确定的拎出来」、l53「我们翻了记录」、l67「那条线，不是他自己画的，是他公司卖的东西画的」。但开场 l02「辞去 CEO 和董事职务，立即生效」、l07「接手这件私事的」、l08「是…把…变成了」偏书面或绕；「我们」几乎每段都有（l08/l09/l23/l30/l38/l39/l53/l58/l62/l63/l64），念稿感重。

V2.evidence: 章节标题「两党都借它追问」「反方怎么说」「留得住的道理」不像口语；l62「这些我们都同意，所以我们从没说过…」「所以」没有因果；l66「这件事留下的道理是：」像结语模板；l21 与 l28「新加坡警方」前说「认定证据不足」、后说「还在查」，听着前后打架。

V3.evidence: l23「是不是跟她」的「她」前面隔了 l22，有女商人、高管两个对象，听不出指谁；l50「据香港〇一转述」听不出是一家媒体；l47「民主党的沃伦」没有头衔；l28 与 l21 的矛盾；l09「没人知道」与 l62「直接原因很可能就是公司治理」口径冲突。

V4.evidence: l52「所以头一天，他的矛头其实是指向民主党的」是 l50 的重复；l65「成了国家安全问题，因为每一方都把它当成国家安全问题在处理」同词绕圈；l15「剩下还有」的「剩下」「还有」重复。其余基本不啰嗦。

V5.evidence: 整体亲切清楚，长短句交替好（l21 长、l22「没有任何人被起诉」短）。但 l16（9.8s）、l18（8.7s）、l65（9.1s）一口气念不完；l12 以逗号收尾、跨句；l07/l08 书面词与 l10/l53 的口语词混用。

V6.evidence: 问题表对每个有点怪或很怪的句子都给了不更长的替换；最别扭 5 句见「整体观察」。

rubric.name: Sounds like a person talking
rubric.question: Each line: natural / a bit off / clearly off. Written-style, lecture tone, translated-from-Chinese phrasing, telegraphic lists all count as off

rubric.name: Flow and transitions
rubric.question: Cold open, the 'what's coming' part, chapter changes, before/after examples: does it sound like one person following a thought, not 'Point one…' templates or a TOC read aloud? Do adjacent lines connect?

rubric.name: Clear on one hearing
rubric.question: Ear only: one new idea per line; clear reference ('this' points to something); terms explained before used; numbers and words not misheard

rubric.name: Tight
rubric.question: No filler, repetition, or empty truisms; point out lines that could go without losing anything

rubric.name: Voice and rhythm
rubric.question: One warm, clear, unpretentious narrator throughout; varied sentence length; each line sayable in one breath

rubric.name: Rewrites
rubric.question: For every 'a bit off' / 'clearly off' line, a drop-in rewrite no longer than the original; rank the 5 most awkward lines

V1.evidence: Most lines are conversational ("Take the tightening side first", "So we checked the record", "don't draw that line too neatly"). Off lines: l07 "the ones who took it up were Nvidia's board...", l06 "On its face, it was a private matter", l69 "When he'll go before Congress is still being worked out", l52 "his first framing was aimed at the Democrats".

V2.evidence: Chapter hand-offs mostly work (l10 "sort what's confirmed from what's only been reported", l24 "here's the real puzzle", l66 "when the headlines fade"). Weak joins: l15 "Then there are two claims" (reads as a timeline step after l14 "he resigned"), l49 "Which is why one popular take..." (does not follow from l48), l40 "so both parties used it to press" (logic implied), l70 ends on a legal disclaimer with no landing.

V3.evidence: Mostly clear, but dense attribution and numbers hurt one-listen comprehension: l16 (8.5s, NYT + unnamed sources + suspicion + Chinese intelligence), l50 (10.8s, HK01 -> Hu Xijin -> Democrats -> Trump), l04 "down more than ten percent... four point three four percent" (screen says -13%), l12 "the target of a foreign intelligence effort" (target for whom?), l21 police "insufficient evidence" vs l28 "Singapore police are still investigating it" can sound contradictory unless you track her vs the company.

V4.evidence: l31 repeats l08; l52 restates l50-51; l09 and l62 both say he did not quit over national security; l38 "for all the shouting" and l32 "same hook" overlap; l36 could fold into l35.

V5.evidence: Too many lines run 9-11 seconds and cannot be said in one breath: l39 (10.4s, two sentences with "Our read:"), l50 (10.8s), l60 (10.0s), l25 (9.6s), l30 (9.6s), l65 (9.6s), l53 (9.2s), l58 (9.2s). Rhythm is long, long, long with few short punches, which is likely behind the "not fluent" feeling. Also l10 is listed at 1.5s for 17 words, which cannot be spoken in that time (pacing check needed).

items.law_name: 中文屏幕文字（PPT 式画面）
items.checks: 逐屏看画面上的中文字：是不是只列纲要、够不够简练、和口播有没有分工、看不看得完。
items.how: 硬上限（超了必须报）：标题 ≤12 字；其余每块 ≤16 字；同屏文字块 ≤4 块（不含页眉小标签、出处与图表刻度）；一屏总字数 ≤36 字。屏幕下方还有口播字幕，观众要同时看。计数口径（第 2 轮裁决定，2026-11-09）：页眉小标签、案例页签、出处、片尾署名不计；同构的列表 / 表格 / 卡片行（每项 ≤8 字、最多 6 项、样子一样）合算 1 块，编号不计字；图里的文字（区域名、曲线名、轴标题、柱条标签、图上注释）要计字数，整张图合算 1 块，只有坐标刻度数字豁免；表格的列头算在表里。
items.what: 逐屏看画面上的中文字：是不是只列纲要、够不够简练、和口播有没有分工、看不看得完。
items.problem: 上一版屏幕文字很多是整句（如「另训一个模型，在两家医院的片子上认医院的准确率——胸片里藏着医院的“指纹”」），等于把口播又印了一遍；用户要求画面只列纲要、相对简练（2026-11-08）。
items.model_why: Claude 单审：a 位评分即最终分，不对比、不裁决

rubric.name: 只列纲要
rubric.question: 每屏只放关键词、短语、关键数字、标签；不是口播整句的复述。按硬上限逐屏数字数，超了就报

rubric.name: 与口播分工
rubric.question: 屏幕给结构、数字、对比，口播负责解释；不和口播逐字重复，也不出现口播没说过的新说法；术语、叫法与口播一致

rubric.name: 层级与体例
rubric.question: 一眼先看到什么、第二眼看什么；标题—要点—注释不超过三级；编号、标签、章节名、目录项前后一致（例：目录写的和章节卡写的是不是同一个说法）

rubric.name: 中文措辞与排版
rubric.question: 短语化、不带句末句号；标点、引号、空格规范；不半中半英；**标题、章名读出来要顺**：名词堆砌、生造的名词短语（如「现实里的祸」）算必改

rubric.name: 看得完
rubric.question: 按截图和停留时间：文字量在停留时间内读得完（约 6 字/秒，还要分神看字幕和图）

rubric.name: 改写
rubric.question: 每处超限或不顺的屏幕文字，都给出更短、可直接替换的写法

P2.evidence: 多数屏幕给结构与数字，口播解释，分工做得好，如 l04「开盘 −13% / 收盘 −4.34%」、l58「有人故意牺牲他：站不住」。小瑕疵：l37 整句引语与口播逐字重复；l40「→ 于是两党都借这件事追问」几乎照抄口播；l05 中英两遍同一句；l41/l42 残留与口播无关的「黄仁勋：丑闻来时在这边」；l63 出现口播未提的「出口管制立法」。

P3.evidence: 「章节号 · 章名」页眉、「我们的判断」标签、已证实 / 未证实标记贯穿全片，层级清楚（l12 起「编号 + h2」列表逐步累加是好设计）。瑕疵：日期写法四种并存（「11 月 9 日」「11-08」「2026-11-08」「11-09 立案」）；22px 的发言人 / 日期小标签（l20「新加坡内政部 · 11 月 12 日」）在 1080p 偏小；章名体例前后不一（问句与陈述混用）。

P4.evidence: 章名「两党都借它追问」「它」无指代，「留得住的道理」是生造的定语短语，两处都属从严必改；l66「私事越不是私事」读着绕；l05 引语句末带句号「我对妻子不忠。」；l02/l03 画面里英文「accepted the resignation」「effective immediately」与中文混排（半中半英）。

P5.evidence: 逐句增量文字停留时间够，如 l56 新增约 11 字、3.0s；l36 新增 10 字、3.0s；l14 新增 7 字、2.2s。但 l13、l21、l22、l29、l55、l56、l60–l65 整屏是累积状态，观众首次扫读、再叠口播字幕时读不完，l62 同屏 12 块（截图可见两张卡片共 7 行）。

items.checks: Screen by screen: is the on-screen English an outline (not prose), tight, divided from the narration, and readable in time?
items.how: Hard limits (report every breach): title ≤6 words; any other block ≤9 words; ≤4 text blocks per screen (not counting the small eyebrow label, source line or chart ticks); ≤22 words per screen. Narration subtitles also sit at the bottom of the frame. Counting rules (round-2 ruling, 2026-11-09): eyebrow labels, case tabs, source lines and end-card credits are exempt; a list, table or card row of look-alike items (each ≤6 words, at most 6 items) counts as one block, and numbering doesn't count as words; in-chart text (zone names, curve names, axis titles, bar labels, callouts) counts toward words and the whole chart counts as one block — only axis tick numbers are exempt; a table's column headers count with the table.
items.what: Screen by screen: is the on-screen English an outline (not prose), tight, divided from the narration, and readable in time?
items.problem: The previous version put full sentences on screen (e.g. 'A separate model identified the hospital for scans from two hospitals — a hospital fingerprint'), repeating the narration. The user wants outline-only, concise slides (2026-11-08).
items.model_why: Claude 单审：a 位评分即最终分，不对比、不裁决

rubric.name: Outline, not prose
rubric.question: Only keywords, short phrases, key numbers, labels; no full narration sentences. Count words per screen against the hard limits

rubric.name: Divided from narration
rubric.question: Screen carries structure, numbers, contrasts; narration explains. No verbatim repetition, no new claims the narration doesn't make; terms match the narration

rubric.name: Hierarchy and consistency
rubric.question: What reads first, second; ≤3 levels (title, point, note); numbering, labels, chapter names and agenda items consistent with each other

rubric.name: Native phrasing and style
rubric.question: Sentence case headline style; no Chinglish; consistent punctuation (no trailing periods on fragments), en dashes, quotes; parallel grammar in lists; **chapter titles and headings must read naturally aloud** — awkward noun stacks are must-fix

rubric.name: Readable in time
rubric.question: From the screenshot and how long it stays: readable in time (~3 words/s while also reading subtitles and the chart)

rubric.name: Rewrites
rubric.question: For every breach or awkward phrase, a shorter drop-in rewrite

P1.evidence: Hard limits are broken on many screens. l61 has about 11 blocks and 49 words (limit 4 blocks, 22 words). l62 has 8 blocks and about 42 words. l65 is about 43 words and l64 about 42. l55 and l47 are about 41, l42 about 40, l60 about 39 and l29 about 36. Cold open l02/l03 carries a 33-word 8-K paragraph (blurred but visible) plus 6-9 other blocks. l37 h2 "Stop fabricating a "spy narrative" / as a pretext for a tech blockade" is 12 words (limit 9) and is a near-verbatim narration quote. l66/l67 h1 "The more critical the product, the less private the life" is 10 words (title limit 6).

P2.evidence: Most screens carry labels and numbers that complement the narration, e.g. l41 "77 : 20", l53 the Nov 9-12 timeline, and l68 "Nov 17 / First earnings without Huang". Repetition: l67 "Who draws the line: what his company sells" is the narration sentence; l37 and l62 "Never said: he quit over security" are close to verbatim. New claim: l04 "−13%" (computed from the open price) is not in the narration, which says "more than ten percent". Wording drift: l09 "Not saying: he quit over national security" vs l62 "Never said: he quit over security".

P3.evidence: The eyebrow "01 · What's confirmed" stays on screen over l15-l22, which are explicitly "reported, not confirmed" claims (l15 "Reported · unnamed sources") and "The other side" rebuttals. The chapter label contradicts the content. Also l16-l18 list items "1 / 2" under that same eyebrow, and "1 2 3" numbering is reused with different meaning across screens. "Our take" pill is applied inconsistently (absent on l39-l47 mid-screens where the take is being made, present on l48). Levels are often 4 (eyebrow, h2 group title, h2 point, body, caption) e.g. l62, l55, l47.

P4.evidence: Sentence case, mostly parallel noun phrases ("Admitted infidelity / Board investigation / Resigned, no reason given"), curly quotes used. Flaws: l60/l62 "Resignation accepted Nov 11, day of report two" is clipped telegraphese ("report two" is unreadable aloud); l25 "Top chips to China? / = the tech war's front line" mixes a question and an equals sign; l22 "Charges: none" plus the duplicate "No charges found as of Nov 14, 2026" and eyebrow "As of Nov 14" say the same thing three times; l09/l62 "Not saying:" and "Never said:" are awkward; l23 "He didn't say · we don't know" is full-sentence prose; chapter title "Both parties press" reads like a headline fragment rather than a chapter name; "China's MFA" (l63) is jargon the narration never says (it says "Foreign Ministry"). Mixed arrows "→" and "=" and ":" as connectors.

P5.evidence: At ~3 words/s, l61 (49 words in 8.1 s, ~6 w/s), l62 (44 words, 7.3 s), l64 (42 words, 5.8 s), l42 (40 words, 6.5 s), l55 (41 words, 6.9 s), l29 (36 words, 3.8 s), l22 (32 words, 2.3 s) and the cold open l02 (60 words, 4.6 s) and l03 (67 words, 3.5 s) cannot be read, and subtitles sit at the bottom as well. On l22 the "Charges: none" text runs past the right edge of its card (screenshot). Most screens carry the previous beats forward, so only the new element needs reading, which softens it, but the new-element text is often still 8-12 words (l60 "Resignation accepted Nov 11, day of report two" in 10 s is fine; l22 shows three new elements in 2.3 s).

P6.evidence: Rewrites below are drop-in and short; every must-fix row has one.
